## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sāriputta Sutta* (Ud 4.7; PTS Ud 43) is a short discourse located in the fourth chapter of the *Udāna* (*Khuddaka Nikāya*), depicting the Venerable Sāriputta absorbed in meditation [SuttaCentral]. The text sets the narrative context for an inspired utterance (*udāna*) uttered by the Buddha on his disciple's mindful composure [SuttaCentral]. Although several discourses in the Pali Canon share the title *Sāriputta Sutta*, search hits in secondary scholarship refer either to the discourse of that name in the *Aṭṭhakavagga* of the *Sutta Nipāta* (Sn 4.16, also known as the *Upatissapañha*) or to a homonymous discourse in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*, leaving this *Udāna* discourse unexamined in the provided literature dossier.
According to SuttaCentral, passage-level parallels to the verse portion of Ud 4.7 are widespread in Buddhist canonical and paracanonical literature, particularly within the *Apramādavarga* / *Purity* chapters of Dharmapada and Udāna recensions [SuttaCentral]. These include the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 4, UVS 4), the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (Uv Kg 4), Chinese translations (T 210.2, T 212.4, T 212.5), and a resembling verse in T 213.4 [SuttaCentral]. Further canonical parallels are identified in the *Theragāthā* (Thag 1.68, *Ekudāniyattheragāthā*), the Vinaya *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Bu-Vb Pc 22), and Turfan and Gilgit manuscript fragments of the Sanskrit Sarvāstivāda and Mūlasarvāstivāda *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* [SuttaCentral].
Automated analysis by DharmaNexus records 61 Pali-internal text reuse matches across 15 texts, primarily reflecting formulaic meditative descriptions and stock phrases [DharmaNexus]. Major reuse partners include the *Ānāpāna Saṁyutta* (SN 54), the *Chakkanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 6), the *Brāhmaṇa Saṁyutta* (SN 7), and the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as closely related portrait suttas in the *Udāna* itself celebrating eminent meditators, such as Ud 3.4 (*Sāriputta Sutta*), Ud 4.6 (*Piṇḍola Sutta*), Ud 4.10 (*Sāriputtaupasama Sutta*), Ud 5.10 (*Cūḷapanthaka Sutta*), and Ud 6.7 (*Subhūti Sutta*) [DharmaNexus].
